magnitude.direction: positive source slope means groundwater level becomes deeper

momentum.measurement_boundary: Aquifer-system comparison companion; it is not represented as a change in the well share.

extent.boundary: Country withdrawal coverage, not a randomized share of global wells, aquifers, land or population.

source_data.derivation: Counts are deterministic filters of the checksum-bound Figure 1 CSV: slope > 0.1, > 0.5, < -0.1 and < -0.5 m/year. Positive slopes mean deepening.
excluded_from_scoring: claim that the monitoring-well sample is randomized or spatially representative

transformations.formula: Count each Figure 1 source-data row with Theil-Sen slope > 0.1 m/year and divide by all 169,717 complete well slopes.
Count each Figure 1 source-data row with Theil-Sen slope > 0.5 m/year and divide by the unchanged source-data denominator.
Use the published 542-system long-history acceleration result only for momentum; do not relabel it as a changing well share.
Use the study-reported approximate withdrawal coverage and preserve its non-random monitoring boundary.

receipts.uncertainty: Well density, monitoring duration, aquifer delineation, datum, screen depth, withdrawals, recharge and national coverage vary. Countries in scope represent about 75% of global groundwater withdrawals but not 75% of aquifers or land. Level decline is not storage volume, depletion attribution or remaining-resource fraction.
receipts.freshness: Primary global in-situ study published 2024; well-level Figure 1 source data checksum 0601fa864de4c2513d3d7df0f55d1c007508446a7d13e40b9a23633d98700dd2; snapshot captured 2026-07-31T19:03:44.479Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: The checksum-bound source data directly supply well-level current magnitude and rapid-threshold exceedance across 169,717 monitoring wells. The same global study supplies multi-decadal aquifer acceleration and country withdrawal coverage, so the current-data gate passes without substituting aquifer prevalence for well prevalence.
